sentences.text: Ricardo Duenas Espriu has served as chief executive officer of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte (OMA) since November 2018, taking the post on November 11, 2018.

sentences.quote: He was Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Grupo Aeroportuario de la Ciudad de Mexico (GACM) from 2015 through 2018 and worked as an advisor in infrastructure projects at the Ministry of Communications and Transportation (SCT) between 2012 and 2015.
sentences.text: He was previously chief financial officer of Grupo Aeroportuario de la Ciudad de Mexico from 2015 to 2018 and an infrastructure project adviser at Mexico's Ministry of Communications and Transportation from 2012 to 2015, after working in JP Morgan's emerging markets investment banking division in London from 2007 to 2011.
As CFO of the Mexico City airport group he was responsible for securing more than eight billion dollars in financing.

sentences.quote: He has an economics degree from Instituto Tecnologico Autonomo de Mexico (ITAM), and holds a MBA from Harvard Business School and a MPA from Harvard Kennedy School.
sentences.text: He holds an economics degree from Instituto Tecnologico Autonomo de Mexico, an MBA from Harvard Business School and an MPA from Harvard Kennedy School.

sentences.quote: known as OMA, is a Mexican airport operator headquartered in San Pedro, near Monterrey, Mexico. It operates 13 airports in the central and northern states of Mexico
sentences.text: OMA, headquartered near Monterrey, operates 13 airports in central and northern Mexico.

mgmt_bio.text: He was previously chief financial officer of Grupo Aeroportuario de la Ciudad de Mexico from 2015 to 2018 and an infrastructure project adviser at Mexico's Ministry of Communications and Transportation from 2012 to 2015, after working in JP Morgan's emerging markets investment banking division in London from 2007 to 2011. He holds an economics degree from Instituto Tecnologico Autonomo de Mexico, an MBA from Harvard Business School and an MPA from Harvard Kennedy School. OMA, headquartered near Monterrey, operates 13 airports in central and northern Mexico.

sentences.text: Ricardo Duenas Espriu was appointed chief executive of OMA in November 2018, working alongside chief financial officer Ruffo Perez Pliego.

sentences.quote: OMA reported strong 2025 operating results with seat capacity up ~11% and total passengers of 28.8 million (+8.5%)
sentences.text: In 2025 the group carried 28.8 million passengers, up 8.5%, with seat capacity up about 11% and adjusted EBITDA of MXN 10.2 billion at a 74.5% margin.

sentences.quote: Management characterized the size of the 2026-2030 commitment as comparable in real terms to the prior 2021-2025 cycle, while noting that current traffic levels are "materially higher" than five years ago.
sentences.text: The civil aviation regulator approved a 2026-2030 Master Development Program of roughly MXN 16 billion, which management presents as comparable in real terms to the 2021-2025 cycle but more capital-efficient per passenger given higher traffic.

mgmt_team_view.text: In 2025 the group carried 28.8 million passengers, up 8.5%, with seat capacity up about 11% and adjusted EBITDA of MXN 10.2 billion at a 74.5% margin. The civil aviation regulator approved a 2026-2030 Master Development Program of roughly MXN 16 billion, which management presents as comparable in real terms to the 2021-2025 cycle but more capital-efficient per passenger given higher traffic. The April 2026 shareholders' meeting approved a Ps.4,900 million dividend in two installments and a Ps.1,500 million Series B repurchase reserve.

sentences.text: Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, known as OMA, operates 13 international airports in central and northern Mexico, including Monterrey.

sentences.quote: Master Development Program 2026-2030 commits Ps. 17,420 million in investments, focusing on capacity, quality, and environmental projects.
sentences.text: Its Master Development Program for 2026-2030 was approved on December 18, 2025, setting maximum tariffs through 2030 adjusted annually by a 0.8% real efficiency factor, with committed investments of 16,005 million pesos.

sentences.quote: Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte (OMA) is investing MX$8 billion (US$480 million) in Monterrey International Airport between 2026 and 2030 to position the facility as Mexico's primary aviation hub.
sentences.text: OMA is investing MX$8 billion in Monterrey International Airport between 2026 and 2030 to position it as Mexico's primary aviation hub.
Second-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA grew 6.2% to MXN 2.7 billion with a 75.2% margin, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA stood at 1.03x.

sentences.quote: Non-aeronautical revenues increased 9.8%, with commercial up 6.7% and diversification up 17.4%.
sentences.text: Non-aeronautical revenues rose 9.8%, with commercial up 6.7% and diversification up 17.4%.

thesis_pillars.text: OMA is investing MX$8 billion in Monterrey International Airport between 2026 and 2030 to position it as Mexico's primary aviation hub. Non-aeronautical revenues rose 9.8%, with commercial up 6.7% and diversification up 17.4%.
